# Voice Trainer — full method and target notes

Long-form companion to https://voice.noravels.com/llms.txt. Everything here is stated in the app
itself as well; nothing is behind a login, and the entire app is a single HTML file.

## 1. What the tool is

Voice Trainer is a client-side web application for practising trans voice (feminine and
androgynous directions, plus a fluid practice mode). It is a static site: no server, no database,
no user accounts, no telemetry. Loading it installs a service worker, after which it works offline.
All state - voice profile, session history, check-in scores, recorded audio - is written to the
browser's localStorage and IndexedDB on the user's own device. Cross-device movement is done by
exporting a single JSON backup (with base64 audio) and importing it elsewhere.

## 2. Learning paths

Practice-first (default): Check-in, Warm-up, Resonance, Register Blend, Volume, Sentences,
Benchmark (weekly), Prosody & Emotion, Fluidity.

Foundation-first (instrument before gender shaping): Play, Pitch stabilisation, Texture
(strong vs soft), Tongue Root, Softness alone, Brightness alone, Blend, Combine (setup), Read.

## 3. The measurement vocabulary used in the app

- Pitch (F0): height of the voice. Displayed as a live line with note names and cents deviation
  from a target, over a 10-second rolling window.
- Resonance: the size and shape of the space the sound vibrates in. Trained via tongue root and
  cavity shape; vocal-tract length and larynx height are what shift formants.
- Register blend: the smooth connection between the strong/heavy and soft/light textures of the
  voice (some teachers say "chest" and "head"), practised with messa di voce glides.
- Vocal weight / phonation: how pressed or relaxed the folds are. In the app this is measured as
  H1-H2 in dB, where a positive value means relatively more first-harmonic energy (breathier,
  lighter adduction) and a negative or near-zero value means pressed.
- Brightness: the balance of high-frequency energy in the sound. Measured in the app as the ratio
  of high-band (2.5-5.5 kHz) to mid/low-band (0.2-1 kHz) energy and shown only as a trend against
  the user's own history.
- Prosody: melody, rhythm, stress and intonation. The most language-specific layer, which is why
  practice material is stored per language.

## 4. Where the numeric targets come from

- Feminine-typical speaking F0 about 180-220 Hz; ambiguous about 140-180 Hz; masculine-typical
  about 100-140 Hz (UCSF Gender Affirming Health Program vocal-health guidance; clinical reviews).
- Speaking F0 explains about 41.6% of perceived gender across 38 studies (Leung, Oates & Chan,
  2018, Journal of Speech, Language and Hearing Research).
- Speech-therapy meta-analysis (2023) reports mean F0 increases of about +27 Hz on sustained /a/,
  +39 Hz in reading and +25 Hz in spontaneous speech after treatment programmes.
- Formants are roughly 20% higher in cis women than cis men; formant frequencies shift measurably
  after 8-12 session programmes (Schwarz et al.; Sodersten et al., summarised in a 2020
  feminisation review, PMC7024865).
- Timbre brightness: the 2-4 kHz band; quantified as spectral centroid / frequency of half energy,
  from about 2.4 kHz in basses to about 3.1 kHz in sopranos (PMC9605961). Perceptual brightness
  correlates with the spectral centroid but is not identical to it (Schubert & Wolfe, UNSW).
- H1-H2: reported range for normal English speakers about +2 to +19 dB (Kreiman, Gerratt &
  Antoñanzas-Barroso 2007, summarised in PMC2997695); breathy vs modal differ by about 4 dB and
  listeners detect differences of roughly 2-4 dB.
- Dose rationale: short daily sessions accumulate the gains above; the app therefore recommends
  15-20 minutes on 5-6 days per week and contains no streak mechanic.

## 5. How profile answers change the session

- Goal: more-feminine / phone-comfort emphasise resonance and brightness prompts; androgynous opens
  the range down to E3 (165 Hz); softer narrows the ceiling and emphasises softness work; explore
  turns off targets and asks the user to compare two versions instead.
- Timbre aim: brighter moves cues to smaller/forward cavity; softer or lighter lowers the ceiling
  to G3 (196 Hz) and restrains volume work; forward moves the focus cue to the front of the mouth;
  natural suppresses exaggerated cues.
- Avoid list: "sounding too high" lowers the ceiling; "strain" additionally reduces volume work to
  a single repetition at a comfortable level; "nasal" adds nasality checks; "artificial" and
  "theatrical" shrink prosody cues.
- Where the voice will be used: the chosen contexts (phone, work, friends, home, daily life) are
  injected as extra speaking prompts.
- Experience: "completely new" or "watched some videos" enables plain-language explanation lines on
  every stage; regular practitioners and therapy clients get the lean interface.
- Practice language: English and Turkish packs today (sentences, emotion prompts, fluidity prompts,
  warm-up vowels, counting, glide material, resonance vowels). Adding a language means adding a pack.

## 6. Safety posture

The app opens every session with a check-in and a pain flag. Elevated fatigue or low comfort adds
"keep it light" guidance to later stages; a pain flag tells the user to skip load-bearing stages.
Persistent hoarseness is described as rest-worthy beyond a day or two and ENT-worthy beyond two
weeks. The app states plainly that it is not medical care or speech therapy.

## 7. Technical facts

Single HTML file, vanilla JavaScript, no frameworks, no external requests (no fonts, analytics or
CDNs). Pitch detection by autocorrelation (or FFT peak in spectrogram mode); spectrogram rendered
on canvas; recordings stored as Blobs in IndexedDB; service worker for offline use and cache
versioning. Licence BSD-3-Clause, forked from Aida Paul's voice-trainer.
